title: The plus-one: why a quarterback who can run adds a blocker (and why Henry had 10 yards without Lamar)
html:
Why this lesson now: the Film Room mirror (football-brief, branch film-room) was checked this run. It still holds one logged game file (data/games/gmum7mktl1wy3.json, "Eagles at Bears, Week 3", no snaps logged) and no review files. The backup source (football-film-room, branch "data") couldn't be read: "repository foolserrandsf/football-film-room is not configured for this session." So there's no new miss of yours to fix. It's a new concept from Monday night, and it builds on Lesson 19 (count the box), which your drill uses on every snap.

The big idea: on a normal run, the QB hands off and is done. He blocks no one.So the offense has 6 blockers (5 linemen and a tight end) and 1 runner.If the defense puts 7 in the box, one defender is never blocked. Coaches call him the plus-one: a free tackler.A QB who can run takes that free man away. The defense has to keep someone home for the QB.

Labels A–D match the steps below. X = defender. The box is the area just behind the defensive line (Lesson 19).

  1. A · The free tackler. QB hands off. 6 blockers, 7 defenders.One linebacker is unblocked. He meets the back at the line.That's what Henry ran into Monday: −1 yard at halftime.
  2. B · Leave one unblocked on purpose. With a running QB, the offense doesn't block the end man. The QB watches him instead. That's called the read.
  3. C · He chases the back, the QB keeps it. The end man crashes inside. The QB pulls the ball and runs outside where he just was.Monday: Justin Herbert ran 22 yards for a TD on the Chargers' first drive. He finished with 7 carries for 51 yards.
  4. D · He stays wide, the back gets it. Now the inside run is 6 blockers on 6 defenders. No free tackler.Omarion Hampton: 22 carries, 105 yards and a TD.

Why Henry had 10 yards: two things went wrong for Baltimore.First, the score. The Chargers led 17-10 at halftime, so the Ravens threw 49 passes (Lesson 51).Second, the plus-one. With Lamar Jackson at QB, every defense has to keep a man home for him. Jacoby Brissett isn't a runner, so the Chargers could send that man at Henry.A run-yards bet on a back whose star running QB is out deserves a smaller number, or no bet.

Tonight's example: Kent State QB Dru DeShields ran for 2 TDs last week. Miami (OH) has to account for him on every run (Kent State hosts Miami, 4:00 p.m. PT, ESPNU).

For your Film Room drill: count the box first, as always. Then ask: can this QB run?QB in shotgun with the back beside him, and the QB is a runner (Lamar, Jalen Hurts, Herbert): the box count is really one better for the offense. Run is more likely.Backup or pocket QB under center: the defense can load the box and dare him to throw. Lean pass on 3rd-and-medium.

Connecting the dots: Lesson 19 counted the box. Lesson 21 showed the option, where the QB decides after the snap. Lesson 33 split QB runs into designed runs, scrambles and sneaks. The plus-one is the math that makes all three work.

Video: search YouTube for "zone read explained plus one" and "Justin Herbert touchdown run Ravens."

Practice it in Football Camp → (Station 2: The box)

quiz.q: The QB hands off. The offense has 6 blockers. The defense has 7 in the box. What happens?
o: One defender is free to tackle the back
The QB blocks the extra man
quiz.w: 6 blockers can't cover 7 defenders. The extra one is the plus-one, a free tackler (step A).

quiz.q: On a read play, who does the offense leave unblocked on purpose?
o: The end man the QB is watching
quiz.w: The QB reads the end man (step B). Whatever he does, the QB does the opposite.

quiz.q: The end man crashes inside to tackle the back. What should the QB do?
quiz.w: He's chasing the back, so the outside is empty. That's how Herbert scored from 22 yards Monday (step C).

quiz.q: Why did losing Lamar Jackson hurt Derrick Henry's running?
o: Defenses no longer had to keep a man home for a QB run
quiz.w: Without a running QB, the defense gets its plus-one back and can send it at Henry.

quiz.q: Film Room: shotgun, back beside a QB who runs well, 6 in the box. Lean?
quiz.w: 6 blockers vs. 6 in the box, plus a QB the defense must account for. The math favors the run.
